pieces.h: Exam Details
pieces.t: Missouri does not use one single statewide journeyman electrician exam for every individual electrician. Journeyman electrician licensing, registration, and testing requirements are commonly set by local jurisdictions. A candidate may need to follow the rules of a city, county, municipal licensing board, local building department, contractor licensing office, or other local authority. A commonly used journeyman-level electrical exam format is the ICC National Standard Journeyman Electrician exam. That exam includes 80 multiple-choice questions, allows 4 hours of testing time, and is open book. Its subject areas include general knowledge, services and service equipment, feeders, branch circuits and conductors, wiring methods and materials, equipment and devices, control devices, motors and generators, and special occupancies, equipment, and conditions.

pieces.h: Open Book Test
pieces.t: The ICC National Standard Journeyman Electrician exam is an open book test. Candidates taking that exam may use approved reference materials during the examination, subject to the exam provider’s rules. Because Missouri journeyman electrician testing is commonly controlled at the local level, candidates must follow the exam-room rules for the specific exam they are scheduled to take. Open book testing still requires strong preparation. The National Electrical Code is a detailed technical reference, and a candidate who is unfamiliar with its structure can lose valuable time searching through unrelated articles. A prepared candidate should be able to identify the subject of the question, locate the correct NEC article or table, interpret the wording, and apply the rule accurately. The included National Electrical Code 2026 Paperback with Tabs is intended to help candidates practice code navigation before exam day.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Missouri journeyman electrician licensing steps depend on the local authority that issues or recognizes the credential. A candidate may need to apply through a city licensing office, county department, municipal board, local building department, contractor licensing office, or electrical licensing authority. Since Missouri does not issue one uniform statewide individual journeyman electrician license, identifying the correct local jurisdiction is the first step. A typical Missouri journeyman electrician path may include completing supervised electrical work experience, finishing apprenticeship or classroom training when required, gathering employer verification, submitting a local application, paying required local fees, scheduling the approved electrical examination, passing the required exam, and completing any remaining local licensing or registration steps.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: Local requirements may include a minimum number of years or hours of electrical experience, proof of work under a licensed electrician or electrical contractor, apprenticeship completion, classroom instruction, identification documents, continuing education, or a local sponsor. Some jurisdictions may recognize an exam passed through a national provider, while others may require a specific local exam or local review process. Missouri statewide electrical contractor licensing is separate from local journeyman-level credentialing. The Office of Statewide Electrical Contractors regulates statewide electrical contractor licenses. A journeyman credential generally supports trade-level work and employment, while contracting authority may require the proper contractor license, business structure, insurance, bonding, and regulatory approval.

pieces.h: Licensing Steps
pieces.t: The Missouri licensing path begins with identifying whether the candidate needs a local individual electrician credential, a statewide electrical contractor license, or both. Individual master electrician and journeyman credentials are commonly handled by local jurisdictions. The statewide electrical contractor license path is handled through Missouri’s Office of Statewide Electrical Contractors. After identifying the correct authority, candidates should confirm the license classification they need. Depending on the location and scope of work, the credential may be called master electrician, journeyman electrician, electrical contractor, electrical registration, municipal license, certificate of competency, or another local title. Each classification may have different application steps, experience requirements, examination rules, renewal rules, insurance requirements, business requirements, and permit privileges.

pieces.h: State Requirements
pieces.t: Missouri uses a mixed licensing structure for electrical work. Many individual electrician licenses are issued locally, while the Office of Statewide Electrical Contractors provides a statewide electrical contractor license path. This means candidates should review both local and statewide requirements before applying, testing, bidding, contracting, or performing electrical work. Local master electrician requirements may apply depending on the city, county, or municipality where the work is performed. A local jurisdiction may control who can pull permits, supervise electrical work, qualify a business, or perform installations. A license accepted in one Missouri jurisdiction may not automatically authorize work in another unless the applicable state or local rules allow it. The statewide electrical contractor license is designed to provide a recognized contractor credential through the state process. Applicants must meet the requirements set by Missouri’s Office of Statewide Electrical Contractors, which may include an approved examination and other application documentation.
